limitations: An original teaching model generated from code, not manufacturer CAD. Proportions, clearances, ports and cooling passages are simplified; the block is cut open so the pistons show. Moving parts are shown at one instant (pistons 1 and 4 at the top). No combustion, flow or load simulation. Explanations drafted by Apex from the listed general references; not yet reviewed by an engineer or clinician.

parts.name: Engine block
parts.purpose: The backbone: holds the four cylinders the pistons slide in, and the crankshaft bearings below. Coolant passages run through it.
parts.connection: The head bolts on top, the oil pan underneath, the timing drive on the front and the flywheel on the back.
parts.model_note: Cut open at the front so the pistons show.

parts.name: Main bearing caps
parts.purpose: Clamp the crankshaft into the block at each main journal, around oil-fed plain bearings.
parts.connection: Bolted to the block bulkheads underneath the crankshaft.

parts.name: Crankshaft
parts.purpose: Turns the up-and-down push of the pistons into rotation. Counterweights balance the offset crankpins.
parts.connection: Connecting rods ride on its crankpins; it drives the flywheel at the back and the timing belt and pulleys at the front.

parts.name: Connecting rods
parts.purpose: Link each piston to the crankshaft, turning straight-line motion into rotation.
parts.connection: Small end on the piston (wrist) pin; big end bolted around a crankpin.

parts.name: Piston 1
parts.purpose: Seals the cylinder and takes the push of the burning mixture. Rings seal gas above and scrape oil below.
parts.connection: Rides in cylinder 1 on a wrist pin and connecting rod. Pistons 1 and 4 move together; shown at the top.

parts.name: Piston 2
parts.purpose: Seals the cylinder and takes the push of the burning mixture.
parts.connection: Rides in cylinder 2. Pistons 2 and 3 move together; shown at the bottom.

parts.name: Piston 3
parts.purpose: Seals the cylinder and takes the push of the burning mixture.
parts.connection: Rides in cylinder 3. Pistons 2 and 3 move together; shown at the bottom.

parts.name: Piston 4
parts.purpose: Seals the cylinder and takes the push of the burning mixture.
parts.connection: Rides in cylinder 4. Pistons 1 and 4 move together; shown at the top.

parts.name: Head gasket
parts.purpose: Seals the joint between block and head against combustion pressure, coolant and oil.
parts.connection: Clamped between the block deck and the cylinder head.

parts.name: Cylinder head
parts.purpose: Closes the top of each cylinder to form the combustion chamber, and carries the ports, valves and camshafts.
parts.connection: Bolted on the block; intake manifold on one side, exhaust on the other.

parts.name: Valves, springs & tappets
parts.purpose: Open and close the ports: intake valves let air and fuel in, exhaust valves let burnt gas out. Springs snap them shut.
parts.connection: Four per cylinder, pushed open by the camshaft lobes through the bucket tappets.
parts.model_note: 16 valves with springs and bucket tappets.

parts.name: Camshafts (intake & exhaust)
parts.purpose: Egg-shaped lobes open each valve at exactly the right moment. One shaft works the intake valves, the other the exhaust.
parts.connection: Driven by the timing belt at half crankshaft speed, since each valve opens once every two turns.

parts.name: Valve cover
parts.purpose: Closes the top of the head and keeps the valvetrain oil in.
parts.connection: Bolted to the cylinder head.

parts.name: Spark plugs & ignition coils
parts.purpose: The coils make a high-voltage pulse; the spark plugs fire it across a gap to ignite the mixture near the top of the compression stroke.
parts.connection: One coil sits on each plug, and each plug screws into the head at the centre of its combustion chamber.

parts.name: Intake manifold & throttle body
parts.purpose: Brings air to each cylinder. The throttle body at its inlet controls how much air, and so how much power.
parts.connection: Bolted to the intake ports on one side of the head.

parts.name: Exhaust manifold
parts.purpose: Collects hot exhaust from each cylinder and merges it into one pipe towards the catalytic converter.
parts.connection: Bolted to the exhaust ports on the other side of the head.

parts.name: Timing belt & sprockets
parts.purpose: Keeps the camshafts in step with the crankshaft so the valves never meet the pistons.
parts.connection: A toothed belt from the crankshaft sprocket around both cam sprockets, the tensioner and here the water pump.

parts.name: Crank pulley, alternator & drive belt
parts.purpose: A separate belt from the crankshaft pulley that drives the alternator (electricity) and other accessories.
parts.connection: On the front of the crankshaft, ahead of the timing belt.

parts.name: Flywheel
parts.purpose: A heavy disc that smooths out the pulses of the power strokes; its ring gear lets the starter motor turn the engine.
parts.connection: Bolted to the back of the crankshaft; the clutch and gearbox attach to it.

parts.name: Oil pan (sump)
parts.purpose: Holds the engine oil at the bottom of the engine, where the pump draws it up.
parts.connection: Bolted under the block.

parts.name: Oil filter
parts.purpose: Cleans the oil of wear particles before it reaches the bearings.
parts.connection: Screws onto the side of the block in the oil circuit.
